metadata.note: The Colorado and Southern's Denver - Cheyenne - Wendover - Orin Junction line: the missing middle of the Burlington system's Texas-to-Montana passenger route. The map already had the two ends - data/fort_worth_denver.geojson (Texas Zephyr, Dallas/Fort Worth - Amarillo - Denver, to 1967) and data/cbq_big_horn_basin_line.geojson (Orin Junction - Casper - Wind River Canyon - Billings, to 1967) - but nothing joined them, so the corridor stopped dead at Denver in one direction and Orin Junction in the other. This layer closes it. Two railroads built it: the Colorado Central ran north from Longmont to the Union Pacific at Hazard, west of Cheyenne, in November 1877, and the Cheyenne and Northern ran 125 miles from Cheyenne to Wendover in 1887; the Union Pacific held both, combined them in the Union Pacific, Denver and Gulf in 1890, and lost them in the 1893 receivership to the Colorado and Southern of 1898, which the Burlington bought in 1908. The through train was the Shoshone, CB&Q/C&S trains 29 and 30, Denver - Billings, 667 miles, gone on September 1 1967 - the same year the Texas Zephyr quit at the other end of the system. Pre-1898 features carry the Union Pacific colour (#F2A900) because the UP owned and ran both predecessors; from 1898 everything is Colorado and Southern in the Burlington colour (#8E1B3C) already used by data/fort_worth_denver.geojson and the CB&Q layers.
geometry_sources: Traced from OpenStreetMap route relations pulled whole from the OSM API: 1421774 BNSF Front Range Subdivision (Denver - Boulder - Longmont - Loveland - Fort Collins - Cheyenne - Chugwater - Wheatland - Wendover) and 7451875 BNSF Canyon Subdivision (Wendover - Orin Junction). Node-id graph, Dijkstra between the terminal towns, Douglas-Peucker at 15 m. Both are the ex-Colorado and Southern alignment, still BNSF freight track.
not_yet_sourced: The year the Union Pacific extended the old Cheyenne and Northern from Wendover to Orin Junction is not pinned down: Wikipedia says only that the UP took the line over in 1887 and 'extended the line slightly to Orin to connect to the Wyoming Central line', and the Wyoming Central reached Casper in 1888. Those 34 miles are therefore drawn only from 1898, with the Colorado and Southern feature - under-drawing them by about a decade rather than inventing a date.

Denver - Longmont before 1898 is not drawn at all here. The through route ran west via Golden until the Denver, Marshall and Boulder line through Broomfield opened in 1886 (standard-gauged 1889), and the Golden routing is a separate corridor that belongs in a Denver-area layer.

No Shoshone timetable was found, so every avg_speed_kmh and every pre-1908 headway_min in this file is an estimate. The train's start date is unknown too - Wikipedia describes its 1946 consist and its 1967 end but not its first run - which is why no named-train feature is drawn for it; the line features carry the service instead.
Whether Denver - Cheyenne carried other passenger service between 1967 and Amtrak's Pioneer in 1977 has not been checked.
metadata.passenger_only_rule: All four features end in 1967 with the Shoshone, not with the railroad: BNSF still runs freight over the whole line. The 1977-1997 Amtrak Pioneer used the Denver - Cheyenne portion and is already drawn in data/amtrak_pioneer.geojson, so it is not repeated here.

properties.speed_source: Estimated. No period timetable was consulted for this line; 40 km/h is a plain guess for 1870s-90s Front Range running.

segments.note: Built by the Colorado Central with Union Pacific backing after construction started in July 1877: the 65-mile connection from Longmont north through Loveland and Fort Collins to Hazard, on the Union Pacific main line just west of Cheyenne, opened for traffic on November 7 1877. It was the first railroad into Fort Collins. Contemporaries complained almost at once about the line’s location and shoddy construction. headway_min is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the July 1877 start, the November 7 1877 opening, the 65-mile figure and the complaints about construction quality are from the UtahRails Colorado Central standard-gauge timeline; the first-railroad-into-Fort-Collins point is from the Fort Collins History Connection. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.

segments.note: Leased to the Union Pacific on March 1 1879 for fifty years, and folded into the Union Pacific, Denver and Gulf Railway when the UP created that subsidiary on March 18 1890 to combine the Colorado Central with the Cheyenne and Northern. The UPD&G went into receivership in the 1893 panic and the property was reorganised into the Colorado and Southern in 1898, where this feature ends and the C&S-coloured one begins.
sources: Segment-level: the March 1 1879 fifty-year lease is from the UtahRails timeline; the March 18 1890 UPD&G formation, the 1893 receivership and the 1898 C&S reorganisation are from the Wikipedia Cheyenne and Northern article. headway_min is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from the BNSF Front Range Subdivision relation (OSM 1421774), cut at Longmont: 75.3 traced miles against the documented 65 miles Longmont - Hazard plus roughly 8 miles Hazard - Cheyenne. Drawn on the present-day alignment. Denver - Longmont is deliberately NOT drawn for this era: until 1886 the through route from Denver ran west via Golden, and the direct line through Broomfield that this layer’s C&S feature uses did not exist yet.

properties.speed_source: Estimated. No period timetable was consulted; 40 km/h is a guess for 1880s-90s Wyoming running.

segments.note: Incorporated in March 1886 by local investors including Governor Francis E. Warren to build from Cheyenne toward northern Wyoming and Montana; about 125 miles of track were laid north through Chugwater and Wheatland before construction stopped at Wendover on the North Platte in 1887. The Union Pacific took the line over that same year, extended it a short distance to Orin to meet the Wyoming Central, and formally put it into the Union Pacific, Denver and Gulf in 1890; it passed to the Colorado and Southern in 1898. headway_min is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the March 1886 incorporation, the 125-mile Cheyenne - Wendover figure, the 1887 halt at Wendover, the UP takeover and short extension to Orin, and the 1890/1898 successions are all from the Wikipedia Cheyenne and Northern article. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from the BNSF Front Range Subdivision relation (OSM 1421774): 117.5 traced miles against the documented 125 miles built, a 6 per cent shortfall that is mostly the Wendover end - the trace stops 1.8 km from the point taken as Wendover. Trace passes within 0.2 km of both Chugwater and Wheatland. The Wendover - Orin Junction extension is not drawn for this era; see the layer metadata.

properties.speed_source: Estimated. The Shoshone covered 667 miles Denver - Billings but no timetable running time for it was found; 55 km/h is a guess consistent with a heavy overnight train making many Front Range stops.

segments.note: The Colorado and Southern was formed in 1898 out of the bankrupt Union Pacific, Denver and Gulf and the Denver, Leadville and Gunnison, and took the Denver - Cheyenne line with it. From 1899 the C&S ran Denver - Boulder over the direct line through Broomfield - the Denver, Marshall and Boulder route of 1886, standard-gauged in 1889 - rather than the older way round via Golden, which is the routing this feature draws. headway_min is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the 1898 formation is from the Wikipedia Colorado and Southern and Cheyenne and Northern articles; the 1886 direct Broomfield line, the 1889 standard-gauging and the 1899 C&S Denver - Boulder service are from the Colorado Encyclopedia’s Broomfield entry. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.

segments.note: The Chicago, Burlington and Quincy bought control of the C&S in 1908, which is what made a Texas-to-Montana Burlington system possible: this line is the middle of it, carrying the Shoshone (trains 29 and 30, Denver - Casper - Wind River Canyon - Billings, 667 miles) which ran until September 1 1967. By its last year the Shoshone was down to a modernised heavyweight coach and storage mail cars. Drawn years end in 1967 with the end of C&S passenger service; Amtrak’s Pioneer used this same Front Range line from 1977 to 1997 and is drawn separately in data/amtrak_pioneer.geojson. headway_min 1440 = the Shoshone’s one train each way daily.
sources: Segment-level: the 1908 CB&Q purchase is from the Wikipedia Colorado and Southern article; the Shoshone’s numbers, 667-mile length, final consist and September 1 1967 discontinuance are from the Wikipedia Shoshone article. avg_speed_kmh is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from the BNSF Front Range Subdivision relation (OSM 1421774): 115.6 traced miles Denver - Cheyenne, on the present-day alignment via Broomfield, Boulder, Longmont, Loveland and Fort Collins - the Shoshone’s own station list. Trace passes within 2.0 km of Boulder, 0.6 km of Loveland and 0.5 km of Fort Collins. No straight-line legs. The Denver end stops 2.1 km short of Denver Union Station, where the trace leaves the relation.

properties.line: Colorado and Southern: Cheyenne – Orin Junction
properties.speed_source: Estimated, same basis as the Denver - Cheyenne feature: no Shoshone timetable running time was found.

segments.note: The old Cheyenne and Northern, plus the short Union Pacific extension from Wendover to Orin Junction, as the Colorado and Southern inherited them in 1898. Orin Junction is where this line met the Burlington’s own Wyoming trackage; the Casper line north from Orin, and the Big Horn Basin route beyond it, are drawn in data/cbq_big_horn_basin_line.geojson and connect to this feature’s north end exactly. headway_min is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the 1898 succession and the UP extension to Orin are from the Wikipedia Cheyenne and Northern article. The exact year the Wendover - Orin extension opened is not sourced - see the layer’s not_yet_sourced field. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.

segments.note: Burlington-controlled from 1908 and the Wyoming half of the Denver - Billings route: the Shoshone came up this line from Cheyenne to Orin Junction before turning north-west for Casper, Thermopolis and the Wind River Canyon. Service ended with the train on September 1 1967. The last scheduled passenger train over the Burlington’s other Wyoming route - Alliance through Sheridan to Billings - ran on August 24 1969, two years later. headway_min 1440 = one train each way daily.
sources: Segment-level: the September 1 1967 Shoshone discontinuance is from the Wikipedia Shoshone article; the August 24 1969 Alliance - Sheridan - Billings last train is from WyoHistory’s Burlington Route article. avg_speed_kmh is an estimate.

The north end lands exactly on the Orin Junction endpoint of cbq-casper-orin-junction in data/cbq_big_horn_basin_line.geojson (0.00 km), so Denver - Billings is now continuous on the map: 115.6 + 151.5 + 398 traced miles = about 665, against the 667 miles Wikipedia gives for the Shoshone. No straight-line legs.
